answer: An agent economy can require each vertex to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. Repeated identities then do not create free influence: an attacker must divide the same capital among them or acquire more stake, and provable fraud can forfeit it. A quill-signed claim may identify the submitting key, while quartz records the stake and slashing evidence; neither label alone prevents Sybils—the binding cost is capital at risk.
